races.name: Molson Coors Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Crokes Cross
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Stuart Coltherd, returning after 87 days; posted a win and placed finish in 3 runs on similar going but zero wins or places in 2 attempts at this sort of pace scenario — likely to be too far back on a track that punishes late closers.
runners_data.comment: Her debut hurdles run at Kelso — a win by one and a quarter lengths at a big price — suggested real ability despite being outpaced early; off for 87 days now but more is expected at this sort of trip on good-to-soft ground. Hard to dismiss despite the break.

runners_data.name: Eremenko
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's five-year-old has won and placed at 20f on Good ground and arrives fresh at 71 days; a natural prominent racer who can sit just off the pace, and his record over this sort of trip in similar conditions is the standout profile in the field.
runners_data.comment: Before her pulled-up run at Bangor, she had won over hurdles and shaped with real promise; stays the trip and handles today's going, and her connections carry a strong record in this race. Returns after 71 days needing a better showing but heads our ratings and has the ability.

runners_data.name: Cinating
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott four-year-old, lightly weighted at 156lbs with a recent win 20 days ago; uncertain style (U) but headgear fitted, and Good ground form shows only flat-course runs — no hurdles form on Good turf yet, making the step to Cartmel's tight turns a genuine unknown.
runners_data.comment: Made amends for a debut fall by landing a maiden hurdle at Roscommon four and a quarter lengths clear last time; a hood is tried for the first time and this filly looks open to further progress. Effective at the trip on good ground — a strong candidate here.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Brian Ellison with a win at 12f on Good ground in form; returned from a fall last time (19F days) which is a significant flag, and the five wins/places from 15 similar-going attempts at a variety of distances suggests a capable but inconsistent type.
runners_data.comment: Making her hurdles debut with nothing directly comparable at this level; held well off the pace at Carlisle on the Flat, beaten six lengths. The trainer is out of form and she is hard to recommend without any hurdling experience under her belt.

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner, trained by Mark Walford and ridden by claimer Tom Midgley; ran just seven days ago and holds a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she is racing slightly out of role here — her ability to control the race is real but winning from front against classier rivals on a fresh turnaround is a discount.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Hexham last time, a step back from her earlier placed efforts; she acts over a longer trip on good ground, so the shorter distance today may not be ideal. A hood is applied for the first time; winless in her last five and hard to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Order Another One
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced five-year-old for Dianne Sayer, style unknown and returning from a pulled-up run 42 days ago; the sole win came last time before the pull-up but the going suitability is flagged as UNKNOWN — significant uncertainty surrounds this runner.
runners_data.comment: Stepped forward to land a maiden point at Ballindenisk by five and a half lengths, bringing some ability from that sphere into rules racing; effective at three miles in points. This is a shorter trip and hurdles are new territory but the potential is there.

runners_data.name: Rachel Lopez
runners_data.note: Stuart Coltherd hold-up mare returning seven days after a pulled-up effort; placed in two of four similar-going runs including at 20f on Good, but the P last time and Sean Quinlan needing to come from off the pace at Cartmel presents a tactical challenge.
runners_data.comment: After a pair of placed hurdles efforts earlier this term, she was pulled up at Hexham most recently; winless in her last five starts but considered a type to improve once eligible for handicaps. Effective at two miles and could still develop.

runners_data.name: Raincloud
runners_data.note: Chapman's six-year-old carries a very low OR of 68 and arrives 36 days after finishing eighth; a genuine hold-up type whose racing position has been pushed forward on the map simply because the rear slots are over-subscribed — tongue-tie fitted, but little in the form to threaten on a Good surface.
runners_data.comment: Reluctant at the start when well beaten at this track last time, a pattern that has characterised recent runs in maidens; without a win in her last five and hard to fancy on current form. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces both applied but consistency has been elusive.

runners_data.name: Big Gypsy King
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for James Moffatt with a fade-in-finish flag attached; the form record shows a string of poor placings in much shorter Flat-code runs, and while the recent hurdles attempt at 17f yielded a fourth, this horse's position in the map reflects overcrowding rather than a genuine ability to race prominently.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 40 lengths when fourth at this course last time, repeatedly showing modest form in maidens; stamina over hurdles also remains unproven at this trip. Winless in her last three outings and our lowest-ranked runner, though her connections have a strong record in this race.

runners_data.name: Echinacea
runners_data.note: Derek Fox aboard Noel Kelly's four-year-old, running off 149lbs with two placed hurdles efforts from 5 runs on similar going; prominent style suits the expected pace scenario and the 37-day break looks a normal preparation — a legitimate each-way profile if she travels as a natural stalker.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Downpatrick last time, beaten 12 lengths but a step forward from her debut in terms of the form she showed; effective at this sort of trip on the prevailing going and heading in the right direction. Winless in her last two starts but a further step forward is plausible.

races.paceDynamic: Millena Agent is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner mares' novice hurdle, and with no serious challenger for the lead, she is set to control proceedings at a sustainable, unforced gallop over the 2m1f Cartmel trip on Good ground. Eremenko and Echinacea are the natural prominent types who will look to track closely, while the bulk of the field — Crokes Cross, Rachel Lopez, Letmeseethecolts — will operate from midfield to rear. The field carries more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate; Big Gypsy King and Raincloud are genuine hold-up horses repositioned on the map to midfield because the rear positions are over-subscribed, meaning neither is likely to secure their preferred ground-saving spot. With Millena Agent able to set a measured pace unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just off the front and pounce at the final flight — Eremenko and Echinacea are best placed to exploit a controlled tempo, while true hold-up runners face the added risk of a turning, undulating Cartmel track that punishes horses who get too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Millena Agent Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Millena Agent gets a clean break and dictates a steady, controlled tempo with no rival applying pressure through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: If Millena Agent gets a clean break and dictates a steady, controlled tempo with no rival applying pressure through the middle stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Eremenko or Echinacea apply early pressure from second or third, forcing a slightly stronger gallop and stretching the hold-up horses before the last.
scenarios.body: If Eremenko or Echinacea apply early pressure from second or third, forcing a slightly stronger gallop and stretching the hold-up horses before the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If Millena Agent sets a truly dawdling pace that compresses the field and allows a late finisher to produce one powerful run up the straight.
scenarios.body: If Millena Agent sets a truly dawdling pace that compresses the field and allows a late finisher to produce one powerful run up the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Millena Agent's controlled lead proves genuinely unassailable and none of the prominent types find the gear to reel her in at the finish.
scenarios.body: If Millena Agent's controlled lead proves genuinely unassailable and none of the prominent types find the gear to reel her in at the finish.

watchPoints.text: Eremenko's jumping must be monitored at the first few hurdles — if he jumps cleanly and slots in behind Millena Agent on the Good ground, his form at 20f and prominent style make him the most dangerous horse in the race as the pace plays directly to his profile.

Millena Agent's seven-day turnaround combined with the STYLE_FIT flag is a meaningful risk factor — if she shows any sign of a flat or laboured jumping display, the uncontested pace scenario collapses and the race opens up for the prominent stalkers behind her.

Order Another One's unknown going suitability and a pulled-up run last time make her a significant X-factor; if she travels well early under Peter Kavanagh, the unknown style could mask latent ability, but any jumping issues could compromise the field's orderly progression.

Big Gypsy King and Raincloud's true hold-up instincts mean they may drift towards the back of the field regardless of where they break — watch early to see if either genuinely pushes forward or drops away, as this will confirm how congested the midfield actually becomes.

Cinating's headgear and recent run form (win 20 days ago) for Gordon Elliott means she is one to watch at the first hurdle for jumping confidence — a clean round from an unknown-style horse with a strong yard behind her could make her competitive if the pace is as steady as expected.

races.name: Burlington Stone Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fine As Wine
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up operator for Gary Hanmer and Sean Bowen, 84 days off the track is a fitness question; has placed twice on similar going in recent starts and handles Good ground, though Cartmel's tight finish can catch out hold-up horses who get a poor draw of traffic at the bend.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Market Rasen last time, beaten 4½ lengths, and she goes well fresh off this 84-day break; effective over a range of trips from 2m to 2m5f and has a decent chance on this evidence, though she is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Caspada
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in the race, Donald McCain's five-year-old carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting it may not get as far forward as usual in this field; on Good ground where it placed second at 2m over similar conditions, it is the key tactical factor for every other runner in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Still in the early stages of his handicap career after struggling on debut at Southwell last time, beaten 9 lengths; effective over 2m on this ground and there is enough potential to keep him on the shortlist, but a clear step up is required.

runners_data.name: Poetry Man
runners_data.note: The Bewley combination saddle an eight-year-old who has placed on Good ground at this trip, headgear applied; as the only other prominent-profile horse in the field he has a clear tactical opportunity to sit just behind Caspada and strike late, though trainer has not hit form in the past 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie and visor fitted after pulling free and over-racing at this course last time, ultimately beaten 8 lengths; the mark is considered fair and he stays well in testing conditions — settling better with the new gear could bring improvement, yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Imperial Rule
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan partners his trainer's horse fresh off a win 36 days ago on Good ground at 2m1f, headgear added; handles this going well with three wins and five places from 14 comparable starts, and his hold-up style suits a scenario where the field arrives together at Cartmel's final bend.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive sort who took a handicap here by a neck last time, off a 4lb higher mark than he carries today; tongue-tie fitted and reverts to hurdles where he can build on that form — effective at this distance on good ground and worth treating with respect.

runners_data.name: Kantagua Du Large
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Clive Boultbee-Brooks with headgear, carries hold-up profile but has yet to place on Good ground from ten attempts in similar conditions — a significant concern; Richie McLernon's booking offers some comfort but the form string shows no win or place at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Tail-ender on our figures who was readily held at Warwick last time having gone forward too soon; tongue-tie and cheekpieces fitted as her mark continues to ease, and she handles this going — but she needs considerably more to get into contention here.

runners_data.name: Ballynoe Boy
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards sends this six-year-old quickly back out after a run 15 days ago; naturally a hold-up horse but the map places it in midfield because the field is packed with runners wanting the rear, meaning it may find itself racing slightly more forward than ideal — STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Outrun at Uttoxeter last time but that effort was clearly about getting a run into him; he should come on from it and acts on this ground over a range of trips — without a win in recent starts but can improve with racing under his belt.

runners_data.name: Masterminding
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's yard is in form (2/7 over 14 days) and this seven-year-old ran second at 2m2f on Good ground last time; the redistribution note means it will likely be racing in slightly more traffic than its natural style would prefer, though that recent good run keeps it relevant if the pace is strong.|
runners_data.comment: Showed up well on handicap debut at this course and distance last time, going down by just 2 lengths off a mark 2lb lower than today's; effective over 2m6f on this ground and must step forward from that promising first handicap start.

runners_data.name: Seeyainthesuninn
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's six-year-old has a low-tier jockey claim (5lb) from Joshua Thompson and has placed once from eleven starts on comparable ground; the redistribution means it will not settle as deep as it would prefer, and nothing in the form suggests it can win from a compromised position.|
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy on the figures after pulling up at Hexham last time, and a clear turnaround in form is required; does act on this ground at around 2m4f and is not without ability, but needs to show far more than he has managed in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Roi Du Roume
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's six-year-old ran just two days ago — a potential stamina concern over 2m6f — though the form string shows four places from eight Good-ground runs; headgear applied and Shane Fenelon (5lb) in the saddle, but the rapid back-up combined with a redistribution from true hold-up position makes this a speculative runner.|
runners_data.comment: Point winner yet to win under rules, and the switch back to hurdles adds uncertainty; was beaten only 2 lengths here two days ago in new headgear, and tongue-tie is added now — the quick turnaround is the main question at this level.

runners_data.name: Path Of Stars
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 2m2f on Good ground for Seamus Mullins, ridden by a 5lb claimer; has placed ten times from fifteen Good-ground starts and the form is solid, though the redistribution means it will be operating slightly more forward than natural — the recent winning form makes it one of the more interesting hold-up types.|
runners_data.comment: Won here 34 days ago, taking a handicap by ¾ length off a mark 8lb lower than she carries today; young enough to have more to offer and her consistent profile makes her the one to beat, though she carries an 8lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — James Moffatt's five-year-old is declared as a non-runner and takes no further part; the redistribution note is moot and its absence slightly reduces the depth of traffic in the hold-up group.|

runners_data.name: Wakey Wakey Man
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — top-weighted at OR=95 for Cian Collins, this six-year-old does not take part; its absence removes the highest-rated horse in the race and simplifies the pace map slightly, leaving Caspada as the clearest pace influence.|

races.paceDynamic: Caspada is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no meaningful pressure anticipated, is set to control from the front at a sustainable gallop over 2m6f on Good ground at Cartmel. Poetry Man is the only other horse carrying a prominent style tag, meaning Caspada should dictate terms entirely unchallenged through the early and middle stages, setting a measured tempo that keeps the race together well into the home straight. The remainder of the field — Fine As Wine, Imperial Rule, Kantagua Du Large and several others — are hold-up types who will need to produce their effort from off the pace late, and Cartmel's tight, undulating track with a short run-in means getting a clear run from deep is far from guaranteed. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with tactical intelligence and course-suited jockeys who can secure a prominent position around the final bend, converting a slow-burn gallop into a sprint finish where those best placed at the top of the straight will have a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caspada Controls; Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Caspada makes all at a sustainable pace and the field arrives bunched turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Caspada makes all at a sustainable pace and the field arrives bunched turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Caspada quickens early in the straight and the hold-up pack is caught flat-footed on Cartmel's short run-in.
scenarios.body: If Caspada quickens early in the straight and the hold-up pack is caught flat-footed on Cartmel's short run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Poetry Man or another prominent tracker sits just off Caspada through the race and strikes at the second-last.
scenarios.body: If Poetry Man or another prominent tracker sits just off Caspada through the race and strikes at the second-last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Caspada sets a genuinely strong gallop that stretches the field and opens the race up for a finisher.
scenarios.body: If Caspada sets a genuinely strong gallop that stretches the field and opens the race up for a finisher.

watchPoints.text: Caspada controls every other runner's race — watch whether Theo Gillard settles for a solo lead or quickens from the second-last, as that single decision dictates whether the hold-up pack has time to close.|

Cartmel's tight left-handed circuit and short home straight compress finishing positions — any hold-up horse that gets trapped wide or behind a wall of rivals turning in is effectively out of the race, so watch the position of Imperial Rule and Path Of Stars at the final bend.|

Roi Du Roume runs just two days after its previous race — watch for any sign of fatigue or laboured jumping in the closing stages, as a tired runner at a hurdle late in the race could cause interference for those finishing strongly.|

With Alvesta and Wakey Wakey Man both declared non-runners, the effective field is ten rather than twelve — watch the revised market to see where the hold-up money lands, as the reduction in bodies through the final bend may open late runs more than the original race shape suggested.|

Path Of Stars is the only hold-up horse in the field with a recent win on identical Good ground and a positive trainer form note — watch whether its 5lb claimer Benjamin Macey can find a prominent enough position early given the redistribution of hold-up types competing for the same rear ground.|

races.name: Campbell & Rowley Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sea The Clouds
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner mapping the pace of this race; the tongue-tie is noted and James Moffatt's stable is in form (2 from 7 last 14 days), but a recent OR=118 finish record of P9-05 suggests vulnerability when pressured late over this trip, and the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 reflects it racing marginally out of natural groove.
runners_data.comment: Veteran hurdler with a mixed recent profile — a winner in his last five but also a pulled-up run — at least held his form when beaten six lengths here last time, though he found less under pressure than his position had suggested. First-time visor; effective at this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Miss Manzor
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained hold-up mare with Sean Bowen up — strong booking — but her recent hurdles form (P56) over shorter trips gives little confidence she'll stay this 2m6f test on Good ground; sim-going figures show 0W0P and she's yet to prove herself at this distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and twice pulled up in that run, she needs to show a sharp upturn here. Last time out she was comfortably held, possibly finding the ground on the quick side; she acts with cut and today's conditions look more agreeable.

runners_data.name: It's All About You
runners_data.note: 292-day absence is the dominant concern here; showed ability at OR=115 and carries cheekpieces and a tongue-tie, but Jennie Candlish's 4 from 21 recent runners is modest and returning hurdlers this far off the track rarely hit peak form first time back.
runners_data.comment: Disappointing on the Flat at Chester last time, well beaten, as he steps back over hurdles; a tongue-tie is on for the first time. Rated 10th on our figures but has shown capability at this sort of trip on any ground and can be given a chance.

runners_data.name: Nakassama
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f at Good going last time out (LR:15d, fresh) and was placed over 2m1f on similar; tongue-tie applied, and the amateur rider (5lb claim) could be a factor in a messy race, but the step up to 2m6f is untested and the sim-going record of 1W2P at this level warrants respect.
runners_data.comment: Performing with confidence under both codes in recent starts — landed a handicap at Downpatrick last time by four and a quarter lengths, stepping up in trip on a mark 14lb below today's. Significantly higher in the weights now and wearing a tongue-tie for the first time, but the confidence is there.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: 13-year-old with a remarkable consistency record — three placed efforts at 2m4f-2m6f on Good or Soft — and a genuine stayer whose Brian Ellison prep (2/31 in 14 days) keeps expectations measured; hold-up style is legitimate here and the trip genuinely suits, though age and handicap mark make a win hard to engineer.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed finisher in his last three completed runs, he looks competitive at this level and suited by the trip and prevailing good ground; first-time cheekpieces are the only change. Trainer form is a concern at present but his form figures point his way and he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Pyramid Place
runners_data.note: Returning from 22 days off over a trip trip shorter than his best; Harry Reed takes the ride and the hist shows 0W0P at this class on Good ground at this range, with most runs on Soft — a tentative hold-up type who needs things to go wrong for others.
runners_data.comment: Jumping form has been patchy of late but his trainer is in good shape and today's trip and ground both suit; a hood and tongue-tie are worn together for the first time. Has shown a tendency to race freely, as he did at Carlisle last time, and settling better is the key requirement.

runners_data.name: Heart Above
runners_data.note: Won over 2m1f at Good last time out (LR:35d), the freshness suits, and Danny McMenamin is a reliable conditional; at OR=107 this trip is slightly further than his best win distance but the sim-going record (2W4P) is the strongest in the field and he travels with clear tactical purpose from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: A horse with a strong affinity for Kelso who landed a handicap narrowly there last time out, showing a return to form at his favoured track on a mark 3lb lower than today's; now steps up in class but handles the ground and trip. Streaky form figures are the one reservation.

runners_data.name: Divilabother
runners_data.note: Exceptional sim-going record of 13 from 15 runs on Good ground and a win over 2m4f at Good last time — Robert Dunne rides and Tristan Davidson sends out 3 from 11 over the fortnight; the strongest profile of any prominent runner for today's conditions and stays the trip.
runners_data.comment: Up in trip at Hexham 15 days ago, patient tactics paid dividends when the early pace collapsed and he landed a handicap by two and a half lengths off a 5lb lower mark; now raised but the trainer is in form. The 2m4f-plus trip clearly suits and the going is fine.

runners_data.name: Feach Amach
runners_data.note: Two wins at 2m1f and 2m5f on Good ground but 87 days off the track is a flag; cheekpieces and a tongue-tie suggest the yard wants to sharpen him up, and Ryan Mania is an excellent jockey for northern tracks, though the layoff makes him harder to trust at face value.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Kelso on her last start, beaten 11 lengths and not threatening the finish; off for 87 days now with tongue-tie and cheekpieces both on for the first time. Effective at this sort of trip on sound ground, but our lowest-ranked runner and has more to do.

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded — natural closers in a field this prominent-heavy often find themselves without the clear ground they need; sim-going record of 0W0P at this level and Lizzie Quinlan's 0 from 3 recent adds caution. The STYLE_FIT flag is deserved.
runners_data.comment: Holds a fair mark judged on Irish form and sits 4th on our ratings, but his last run here was a let-down despite being well-positioned — comfortably held when the race was there for the taking. First-time tongue-tie and visor are the response; inconsistency remains the key risk.

runners_data.name: Evenwood Sonofagun
runners_data.note: Won over 2m6f at Good going earlier this season and placed again over the same trip — the distance profile is the best in this race; Sean Quinlan is an experienced northern jumps rider and the Lizzie Quinlan stable pair here adds interest, though 0 from 3 in 14 days keeps the yard angle modest.
runners_data.comment: Running with renewed purpose and only denied by a neck last time off a mark 4lb lower than today's, doing everything right until run out of it in the closing stages; that tendency to find little late is the concern. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied; the mark still looks workable.

runners_data.name: Secret Secret
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner that the map has pushed toward midfield because there are too many prominent types in this field; Brian Hughes is a top jockey but a 10-year-old with 0W1P sim-going and recent form of 469-54 is asking for confidence the evidence doesn't support, especially racing out of role. STYLE_FIT 0.93.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts and ranked 12th of 13 on our figures, the better-fancied rivals look ahead of him here; but he did show some encouragement at this track last time, keeping on to finish fourth, beaten seven and a quarter lengths. A tongue-tie is applied today.

runners_data.name: Jack Sprat
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which immediately raises freshness concerns at 2m6f; a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield — in practice, he may struggle to find the back of the field and the combination of quick turnaround, STYLE_FIT 0.91, and 0W3P sim-going makes this a very difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Second here in a chase last time out, beaten three lengths off this same mark, showing his best form — a versatile type capable of going well back over hurdles. Winless in his last five outings and first-time cheekpieces on today, but the course and trip suit.

runners_data.name: Butty O Brien
runners_data.note: Listed as non-runner; a naturally prominent type who would have added to the pace congestion had he run — his absence slightly eases the pressure on Sea The Clouds and benefits the settled prominent runners like Heart Above and Divilabother. No further relevance to the race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Sea The Clouds is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, should dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good ground at Cartmel. Heart Above, Divilabother, Feach Amach, and It's All About You are all prominent-style runners who will look to sit close to the leader, creating a bunched, competitive head of the field rather than a true pace duel. The field is front-heavy: Butty O Brien and Secret Secret are natural prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred berth, while Rauzan and Jack Sprat are genuine hold-up horses displaced toward the middle of the map — none of these should be expected to produce hold-up finishing kicks as true closers would. With a sustainable, uncontested tempo and several horses pressing from just off the pace, this race shape most strongly favours horses who travel prominently, stay the trip well on Good ground, and possess the stamina to kick on from the front of the field rather than those relying on a late run from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sea The Clouds sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the prominent pack tracks without burning excessive petrol.
scenarios.body: If Sea The Clouds sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the prominent pack tracks without burning excessive petrol.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent runners applies sustained pressure that eventually overpowers Sea The Clouds in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of prominent runners applies sustained pressure that eventually overpowers Sea The Clouds in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough and sustained deep into the race to open ground for a closer to pick off the tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough and sustained deep into the race to open ground for a closer to pick off the tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field breaks up early, pace collapses mid-race, or prominent horses burn each other out unevenly.
scenarios.body: If the field breaks up early, pace collapses mid-race, or prominent horses burn each other out unevenly.

watchPoints.text: Divilabother's Good-ground sim record of 13/15 and recent 2m4f win make him the standout pace-shape fit — watch whether Robert Dunne positions him directly behind Sea The Clouds from the off, as that's the ideal seat in this race.

Heart Above is freshened (35 days), won last time at Good, and Danny McMenamin will look to travel prominently; if he tracks Sea The Clouds into the straight, his stamina and sim-going form (2W4P) put him right in the argument.

Jack Sprat ran only two days ago — watch for any signs of physical fatigue or ring-rustiness in the parade ring and early on; a horse with a quick turnaround over this stamina trip is a notable race-integrity flag.

The cluster of prominent types — Heart Above, Divilabother, Feach Amach, It's All About You — will all want the same ground behind Sea The Clouds; watch the first two furlongs to see who actually secures that position, as those shuffled back early are significantly disadvantaged.

Evenwood Sonofagun has the best distance profile in the field (won at 2m6f Good) and Sean Quinlan is an informed booking — if he jumps well and settles smoothly in mid-prominent, he's the most likely improver to emerge late from just off the pace.

races.name: Oakmere Homes Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Zillow
runners_data.note: Recent form is patchy (F00 in last three) but has a winning run on Good ground at 16f in similar company; prominent style suits the expected race shape and Brian Hughes gives the booking a practical edge, though the 85-day absence after those poor efforts is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Tail-ender on our figures after finishing well beaten when stepped up in class in a Listed handicap hurdle at Fairyhouse on his last outing; the class drop helps and he acts with cut over this trip, but a significant turnaround is required from that effort.

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning on 34-day break, and his Good-ground record shows 0 wins and 0 places from nine attempts — the style and going profile here both work against him, and the 5lb headgear flag adds a layer of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Cartmel specialist who has taken this race in each of the past three seasons; first-time cheekpieces fitted after failing to stay the trip at Ballinrobe latest, and he drops to a mark 2lb lower than 12 months ago — the course record makes him hard to oppose.

runners_data.name: High Court Cave
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, who has a solid Good-ground record (1W2P in 6 runs) and the benefit of a 5lb claimer keeping the weight down; he shapes as the pace-setter throughout but must convert a controlled lead as the field tracks him closely.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces for this one, who has shown promise based on his bumper profile; beaten 9 lengths stepping up in trip at Listowel last time, but the drop back to a more suitable distance could suit and there may yet be scope for further progress in handicap hurdles.

runners_data.name: Filibustering
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground (16f and 17f) make this five-year-old's recent form compelling, and Harry Derham's T14 stat of 1/1 is a strong signal; the prominent style fits the expected race shape perfectly and the trip appears well within range.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back hurdles successes mark him as a genuine contender here and he handles this trip and going well enough; below par on a Flat start at Kempton but that effort can be set aside, and the tongue-tie is new.

runners_data.name: Miss Maverick
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground from recent prominent-style efforts, including a win over 20f, and the 15-day turnaround suggests she is in a training peak; James Davies rides and she has the experience at this distance to mount a sustained challenge from close to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Front-running mare who was overhauled well beaten off 124 last time having gone too hard too soon; drops 2lb here and is effective at this distance on sound ground, but a degree of caution is needed given that recent effort.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: In-form bumper/hurdles winner with two wins on similar ground, but this natural front-runner finds himself squeezed out of prominent position by the volume of pace in the field — the style-fit flag (0.93) and 197-day absence dampen what looks an attractive profile on paper.
runners_data.comment: A front-runner who showed tremendous resolve to edge a handicap at Carlisle last time, winning by a short-head off a 44lb lower mark; back over hurdles now with the tongue-tie fitted and very much in the mix over this trip and going.

runners_data.name: Banderas
runners_data.note: Two hurdle wins on Good ground and a consistent record makes him interesting from a hold-up position; Richie McLernon is a good fit and the 13f freshener flag (fast ground) is notable, but he needs the pace to be searched and is reliant on the front collapsing.
runners_data.comment: Struggles to feature on our figures given the 44lb jump from his last Flat run; effective over this trip on similar ground and the tongue-tie is new, while connections are in decent nick — worth a second look at bigger prices.

runners_data.name: Nap Hand
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on Good ground (seven places in ten runs on similar going) but no wins at this distance/going combination; Tom Cannon is an upgrade booking but the hold-up style requires the race to develop very differently from the expected shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed across both codes and shapes as a genuine each-way threat, having finished just over 2 lengths adrift at Salisbury last time off a 32lb lower mark; without a win in recent starts and the yard is out of form, but the profile warrants respect.

runners_data.name: Bittalemon
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse who has been redistributed to a midfield label — the 0.93 style-fit flag acknowledges he races out of his natural deep position here; the Leah Noreci 10lb claim helps with weight, but the five-year-old's best run (17f, Good) came when able to settle further back than likely here.
runners_data.comment: Showed her stamina when beaten 2½ lengths here last time after dropping in class; has the form at this course and distance, and first-time cheekpieces could spark further improvement — she is capable of a say.

runners_data.name: Winds Of Winter
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground at 16f recently but ran just seven days ago, and this genuine prominent type cannot get his natural position in a field stacked with pace — the 0.92 style-fit flag and fresh-run concern combine to make his chance structurally compromised regardless of ability.
runners_data.comment: Racing off a mark above her last success but has shaped with promise in recent outings; over-exerted herself in front at Hexham last time, beaten 3½ lengths on this mark, and a more patient approach could help — winless in recent starts but worth watching.

runners_data.name: Goodwin Face
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins and a string of places on Good ground give Sean Bowen an attractive horse on form alone (2W5P in 9 runs on similar going); however, this natural prominent racer is pushed out of his preferred position by the crowded pace, and the two-day turnaround after his last run is worth monitoring despite the positive booking.
runners_data.comment: Back here just two days after landing a handicap by 7 lengths at this course and clearly in fine fettle; the progressive profile makes him a threat but he carries a 7lb penalty this time and the quick turnaround needs to hold up.

races.paceDynamic: High Court Cave is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an 11-runner field, this race is set to be run at a sustainable, controlled gallop from the front — nobody is likely to seriously test High Court Cave for the lead, meaning the pace will be honest but not searching. Filibustering, Miss Maverick, and Zillow are natural prominent racers who should track closely in second, third, and fourth, giving the race a clearly defined shape with the leaders dictating terms throughout. Amancio, Goodwin Face, and Winds Of Winter are genuine prominent types who will be unable to secure their natural position and will be shuffled into midfield roles they do not naturally fill, reducing their effectiveness and making their redistribution flags relevant to any assessment. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured pace on Good ground over 2m1f at Cartmel's tight track — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort to the line, with true hold-up horses unlikely to generate the momentum required to reel in a controlled front-running display.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If High Court Cave bowls along at a sustainable gallop and the prominent racers immediately behind deliver a measured challenge from two out.
scenarios.body: If High Court Cave bowls along at a sustainable gallop and the prominent racers immediately behind deliver a measured challenge from two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On, Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely uncontested and High Court Cave converts his front-running role into a wire-to-wire success on the tight Cartmel track.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuinely uncontested and High Court Cave converts his front-running role into a wire-to-wire success on the tight Cartmel track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than expected and the leaders tie each other up, giving a genuine hold-up horse ground to make.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves faster than expected and the leaders tie each other up, giving a genuine hold-up horse ground to make.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the demoted prominent types — Goodwin Face or Amancio — manages to slot closer than their mapped position and benefits from a collapse in the front rank.
scenarios.body: If one of the demoted prominent types — Goodwin Face or Amancio — manages to slot closer than their mapped position and benefits from a collapse in the front rank.

watchPoints.text: Filibustering and Miss Maverick are both confirmed prominent types with recent wins on Good ground — if either settles directly behind High Court Cave from the outset they are the two most dangerous horses in the race given the expected controlled pace shape.
Goodwin Face ran just two days ago; Sean Bowen's booking is a positive signal but monitor market moves and any reports of freshness concerns before committing to this horse's chance.

Amancio has been absent 197 days (including a fast-ground run flagged); despite a strong profile on form, the combination of that layoff, style redistribution, and a field too full of pace for him to get his natural position means he carries meaningful first-time-back risk.

Cartmel's tight, turning track historically punishes hold-up horses who cannot get a clear run through — Banderas, Nap Hand, and Bittalemon all need a smooth passage and the pace to collapse, both of which are low-probability outcomes in this race shape.

High Court Cave's amateur rider Mr O McGill carries a 5lb claim, reducing his weight to 158lbs; if he settles the horse into an uncontested lead on the Good surface, the question is whether the concession of ground and the tight Cartmel turns become factors late in the race.

races.name: Oakmere Homes Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pour Les Filles
runners_data.note: Back on good ground which suits (6/13 similar-going record, 1W5P), Mickey Bowen in form (3/12), wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and gets an unchallenged lead — her STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is technically mapped as prominent here, but she is the confirmed front-runner and race controller, so her chance is real if the lead is not pressured.
runners_data.comment: Kept on for third at this course last time, 6 lengths off the winner despite struggling to land a blow from his position; tongue-tie fitted for this return, works well over this ground and trip, and the mark remains workable — inconsistency for the new yard is the main caveat.

runners_data.name: Light N Strike
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for the same Bowen yard with solid good-ground figures (12/15, 2W7P) but has a string of placed efforts (UP0-46 recent form) suggesting he is competitive without always clinching; wears blinkers, 10yo at OR 130, and carries top weight, which may blunt his finishing effort late on.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well at Perth last time when failing to stay the distance; drops back to his preferred shorter range now with first-time blinkers and carries a mark below his best — the trainer is in good nick but he is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (251-32) with a course-distance win in the mix, and his good-ground numbers (9/15, 1W6P) back him up — genuinely wants to race prominently and is one of the likelier of the redistributed trio to push forward and secure a handy berth; tongue-tie and visor fitted, and Tristan Davidson's yard is in a small run of form (3/11 T14).
runners_data.comment: Narrowly held last time, going down by ¾ length off 123 before his stamina faded late; 4lb higher here but visor fitted and effective over this range of trips on decent ground — in good recent order and has every chance if the mark doesn't prove too stiff.

runners_data.name: Buy Some Time
runners_data.note: Won over C&D trip last time (1/24f/GOO) and has the best good-ground record in the field (9/15, 4W6P), which is the standout statistical angle here; a front-running type at heart who has been mapped to midfield through redistribution, but expect Ryan Mania to push forward — headgear (hood/tongue-tie) has been consistent, and this trip and ground is his sweet spot.
runners_data.comment: Won over fences at Perth last time by 6 lengths off a 7lb lower mark; hood and tongue-tie now fitted and he's generally consistent over this range of trips — 7lb higher but there could be further improvement to come back over fences and hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Got Grey
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the race, which makes her an outlier in this pace shape; good-ground experience is solid (13/15) but she needs the pace to truly soften up the leaders and 10lb claimer Leah Noreci is untested at this level — step up from 18f to 21f is a query.
runners_data.comment: Finished 4½ lengths off the pace at this course last time and his best hurdle figures suggest he's on a workable mark; tongue-tie fitted and effective over this trip on good ground — should go well if producing close to his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on good last time out (1/21f/GOO) and returns at OR 108 with claims, but as a displaced prominent type he is unlikely to get the rail-hugging prominent pitch he needs; Dianne Sayer's stable is quiet (0/3 T14) and the redistribution means Sean Quinlan may find himself further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: A horse who clearly thrives at this venue and put in a dominant display last time here, taking a handicap by 5½ lengths off a 7lb lower mark; consistent type effective at this trip and connections have taken the past two editions of this race — he looks a serious threat to the favourite.

races.paceDynamic: Pour Les Filles is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners and no genuine rival to press her, she is set to control this from the front at a sustainable, unflustered gallop over 2m5f on good ground at Cartmel. The field is unusually packed with prominent-running types — Breizh River, Buy Some Time, and Sean Og are all natural front-to-prominent racers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all get their natural position behind Pour Les Filles; of these, Breizh River (OR 127, strong recent form) and Buy Some Time (OR 114, won over C&D trip) are most likely to push forward and sit closest to the pace. With the front-running Pour Les Filles allowed to bowl along uncontested at her own tempo, the gallop is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically favours horses travelling prominently with tactical speed rather than deep closers who need a genuine test. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile — horses tracking the early pace with fluency and the ability to pick up in the home straight — and disadvantages true hold-up types who need the race to be truly run to suit a late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Sets Up Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race lacks a strong injected surge to stretch the field.
scenarios.body: If Pour Les Filles dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race lacks a strong injected surge to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles builds a decisive advantage jumping the final fences and none of the prominent chasers can sustain the effort up the run-in.
scenarios.body: If Pour Les Filles builds a decisive advantage jumping the final fences and none of the prominent chasers can sustain the effort up the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Causes Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types jostle for position early, creating a contested pace and a more searching race than expected.
scenarios.body: If the surplus of prominent types jostle for position early, creating a contested pace and a more searching race than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late challenge and Got Grey travels powerfully off the bridle into contention.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late challenge and Got Grey travels powerfully off the bridle into contention.

watchPoints.text: Breizh River and Buy Some Time are both natural front-runners squeezed into midfield on the map — watch the first three fences to see if either pushes forward aggressively and alters the expected pace picture entirely.

Pour Les Filles has a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she is technically mapped prominent; if she is not first to the first fence and another horse takes the lead, her chance diminishes sharply as she loses her key tactical asset.

Got Grey is the sole hold-up horse and her chance is almost entirely dependent on the redistributed runners forcing a contested pace — if the field settles in a single-file pattern behind Pour Les Filles, she will struggle to get into contention.

Light N Strike has run 0 from 3 starts in his last five finishes (UP0-46 form) — watch whether Sean Bowen's stablemate presses for the lead or sits in behind Pour Les Filles, as their shared yard may have a preference for which leads.

Cartmel's tight, undulating track heavily rewards clean jumping and positional awareness — any of the prominent types who make a jumping error at the cross-fence or the dip will likely surrender their position permanently.

races.name: Holker Hall & Gardens Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter in the race and likely to lead unchallenged; ten-year-old trained in Ireland, 15 days since last run, tongue-strap fitted, but his Good-ground similar-going record of 1W2P from 11 runs offers modest encouragement, and at OR 100 he carries the burden of a horse who rarely gets to dictate like this.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five and ranked 9th of 10 on our figures, his recent handicap form has been modest — a well-beaten effort at Downpatrick last time where he was pressed too hard too soon. Tongue-tie and cheekpieces on for the first time; his hunter-chase figures will not translate directly to this level.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent racer returning from a 143-day absence for Brian Ellison, whose 14-day strike rate of 2/31 merits mild caution; all five recent runs have come on Soft or Heavy and this Good ground is an untested variable that cannot be overlooked.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for 143 days after being pulled up at Doncaster; first-time cheekpieces as he returns to competition. His two recent wins came over different codes and the trip and going suit, but the current chase mark asks more after a lengthy absence and the form requires updating.

runners_data.name: Halfway House Lad
runners_data.note: Two wins from his last five including back-to-back successes on Good ground at 24f and 26f, making him the most course-and-condition-relevant prominent horse in the field; James Moffatt's yard is in form at 2/7 over 14 days and Leah Noreci's 10lb claim reduces the burden meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Two wins on the bounce and clearly in fine form — the latest a narrow success here under a positive front-running ride at a 7lb lower mark. Raised again in the weights but the course, trip and good ground all suit; tongue-tie on first time. Looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap and blinkers fitted, OR 84, ran just 2 days ago which raises freshness concerns in a 3m1½f chase; his recent record shows three pulled-ups or unfinished efforts and his Good-ground form of 1W1P from 6 runs is unremarkable for this level.
runners_data.comment: Course form from 12 months ago is genuinely appealing — he landed this race last year — and today's trip and going suit; blinkers and tongue-tie applied first time in an attempt to reverse a run of poor recent efforts. His most recent start here was well below that earlier level.

runners_data.name: Lights Are Green
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature whose preference to race handy is frustrated here by the volume of similar-styled horses — he is likely to sit further back than ideal; that said, 11 runs on similar going underline he handles this surface and his last completed run on Good ground was a third at 26f.
runners_data.comment: Third at this trip and going when things went right in his last five starts, but also pulled up on three occasions; he has a history of not applying himself fully and that unreliability makes him difficult to trust. Winless in his last five and ranked mid-field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: Wants to race prominently but finds the race shape working against him, pushed into a midfield slot he does not naturally inhabit; his recent form figures include two unseated-rider entries and a fifth at a far shorter trip, and John Dixon training and riding is a small-stable angle worth noting at 0/0 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Parted company with his rider early at this track last time out, adding to consecutive unseating runs; our lowest-ranked runner with plenty to prove and winless in recent starts. First-time cheekpieces and he handles sound ground, but more secure jumping is essential.

runners_data.name: Star Turn
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse ridden by Sean Bowen for his father Mickey, which is a potent combination; back-to-back placed efforts over 24f on Good and Soft give him credibility at this trip and on this surface, though 54 days off and a tongue-strap plus blinkers combination suggests he needed those runs to sharpen up.
runners_data.comment: Second in a handicap hurdle last time, settling for the scraps before keeping on to go under by 10 lengths; back chasing now with first-time blinkers after 54 days away. Winless in his last four starts and has more to prove over fences, though the trip and going suit.

runners_data.name: Croagh Patrick
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up horse who showed a second on Good ground over 24f on his most recent start; Sean Quinlan takes the ride and he handles this going on a form basis, but his record of 0W2P from 9 similar-going runs and age make him a horse to respect rather than fear.
runners_data.comment: A step in the right direction at Hexham last time, beaten just two lengths off a mark 2lb lower than today's; first-time blinkers are applied. Unreliable on his record — twice pulled up in his last five — but his better efforts suggest the handicapper has been lenient at this trip.

runners_data.name: Aill Dubh
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose entire recent history is on Soft or Heavy — five of his last five runs coming in those conditions — making Good ground a genuine unknown despite his course-trip form in theory; Micky Hammond's yard is at 0/9 over 14 days which adds no confidence.
runners_data.comment: Racing prominently last time, he gave the closers too much room and was beaten 11 lengths off a mark 2lb above today's; first-time cheekpieces and a trainer in form. Point-to-point ability suggests there is more in the locker than his hurdles mark reflects — a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Kingofthegame
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on Good ground last time out for Ryan Mania and is a naturally prominent horse whose best form comes from racing close to the pace; the redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded prominent group, not his optimal race shape, and if he gets loose in the right position his Good-ground trip record (1W2P from 7 runs) makes him a factor.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap here last time by a neck off a mark just 1lb above today's, and his profile is clearly on an upward curve; the course, trip and going all suit and he arrives on a fractionally lower mark today. A genuine danger to the selection.

races.paceDynamic: Shantou Show is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap chase over 3m1½f at Cartmel, and with no other genuine pace horse to press him, he is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop that plays firmly to his strengths. The field is laden with prominent types — Lights Are Green, Blazing Court, and Kingofthegame all want to race handy but cannot all occupy that territory, meaning at least two will be shuffled back and racing in an unfamiliar gear. With Shantou Show setting an uncontested tempo and the Good ground rewarding jumping fluency over raw finishing kick, horses who can travel close to the pace without burning energy in a positional battle will be best placed. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours genuine prominent racers who secure a natural position early and jump cleanly, with hold-up horses facing a stern test of whether they can close on a leader who has never been threatened.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shantou Show Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Shantou Show leads unchallenged and the redistributed prominent types fail to assert, setting a controlled pace that stretches the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: If Shantou Show leads unchallenged and the redistributed prominent types fail to assert, setting a controlled pace that stretches the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Heats Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Blazing Court or Lights Are Green pushes forward aggressively early, forcing a more genuine gallop that tests Shantou Show's stamina at this 3m1½f trip.
scenarios.body: If Blazing Court or Lights Are Green pushes forward aggressively early, forcing a more genuine gallop that tests Shantou Show's stamina at this 3m1½f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough throughout and the field strings out, leaving room for the true hold-up types to deliver a finishing effort.
scenarios.body: If the pace is honest enough throughout and the field strings out, leaving room for the true hold-up types to deliver a finishing effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Outfox Field
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution resolves itself early with Lights Are Green or Kingofthegame securing a prominent berth, effectively turning the front of the race into a multi-horse group.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution resolves itself early with Lights Are Green or Kingofthegame securing a prominent berth, effectively turning the front of the race into a multi-horse group.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Blazing Court or Lights Are Green attempt to push forward at the start — if either challenges Shantou Show for the lead, the tempo will rise sharply and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Judicial Review ran just 2 days ago and is fitted with both tongue-strap and blinkers; Brian Hughes is a high-class jockey but a horse this fresh off a run in a 3m1½f chase deserves monitoring at the first few fences for jumping fluency.

You Did returns from 143 days off and all recent form has come on Soft or Heavy — watch his early movement on Good ground, as any signs of stiffness or lack of fluency jumping could see him fade from a prominent position quickly.

Halfway House Lad's back-to-back wins on Good ground at distances matching today's trip make him the standout form horse for the prevailing conditions — watch whether Leah Noreci holds him up early or commits to tracking Shantou Show, as her positional choice will be decisive.

Star Turn is the most credible hold-up threat if a genuine pace develops — monitor whether Sean Bowen settles him in the rear and saves ground on the final circuit, as his two recent placed efforts on Good ground suggest he has the class to close if the leaders tire.

races.name: Women's Community Matters Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Conquer The Breeze
runners_data.note: Sharp prominent racer returning just seven days after winning, Adam Nicol yard in excellent nick (T14: 1/6), and the good ground suits — 2W7P in similar conditions; top weight at 172lbs is the one check but recent form figures of 1-1-4-1 demand respect.
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last five, including a 7-length handicap success at Hexham last week; carries a penalty here with the tongue-tie fitted, and a repeat would be impressive — clearly in good heart but the higher weight asks more.

runners_data.name: Fort Randall
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been off 44 days; amateur rider Mr O McGill (5lb claim) could be an asset in a smaller-field handicap, and the horse's three good-ground chasing seconds show he handles conditions — needs a truly-run race to deliver off the back end.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with credit on the hurdles last time, finishing 5¼ lengths off the pace off a revised mark; 2lb higher here but back over fences where he may be better suited, and he acts on this going — a genuine each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up mare trained by Sam England, arriving 15 days after a win with Sean Bowen booked — a powerful combination; good ground form reads well (1W3P) and the headgear flag suggests she's been sharpened up, but she needs something to aim at turning for home.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who took a handicap at Hexham by 3 lengths off a 4lb lower mark last time and runs off the same official mark here; handles this ground and distance well and the trainer is in form — well worth including.

runners_data.name: Intenzo
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type, five-year-old with a strong strike rate on good ground (7/9 in similar conditions) despite no wins at this track; Jamie Walford yard has had some placing form this fortnight and at 2/18 this could represent a tightening angle — exposed at the top level but game.
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie fitted for the first time and shaped with renewed intent at Market Rasen last time, beaten just 2½ lengths off a 1lb lower mark; yet to win in recent starts but handles this trip and a good run is not out of the question.

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice on good ground in 15 runs (2W6P) and arrives 22 days fresh; Danny McMenamin rides for Brian Ellison and recent form 5-3-9-3-8 shows she hits the frame periodically but does not consistently go close — likely to fill the third or fourth berth if the pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Took a step back at Hexham, jumping poorly and well beaten when tried over a longer trip; more effective at 2m on this ground and the drop back in distance could help, though the trainer is out of form and a turnaround is needed.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Arrived at this race off a win (6-7-4-5-1 recently) over slightly further on good ground — the form line is live; prominent style suits in a race with a single pacemaker, Danny Gilligan is a capable claimer, but trainer Collins has no strike from 3 runners in the past fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Had been frustrating before getting off the mark at Kilbeggan last time, winning by 2½ lengths off a 10lb lower mark; tongue-tie and cheekpieces now fitted as he returns to fences — the scope is there to build on that now he has broken his duck.

runners_data.name: Bentley Road
runners_data.note: The only true front-runner in the race, Derek Fox takes over on a horse whose best going figures come on good ground (2/4) and who drops back to a more suitable 2m1½f after two runs at 3m; she sets the race shape but her OR of 96 and limited winning form means she will be caught if rivals travel smoothly in behind.
runners_data.comment: Shaped better at Hexham last time under a positive ride, beaten 3 lengths off this mark on a stiffer track; cheekpieces fitted and effective across a range of trips — winless in recent starts but must carry that effort forward.

runners_data.name: Cuzco Du Mathan
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up handler in visored headgear whose natural place is at the rear; in a field with three other genuine hold-up types, James Moffatt's runner will struggle to get the clean passage he needs — form of 7-6-4-4-7 underlines that he rarely threatens on good ground and his chances are compressed by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Drops in the weights after a run of modest results and the ground was too fast when well beaten here last time; visor fitted now and he clearly needs ease in the ground — if conditions soften enough, his best form puts him right in the picture.

runners_data.name: Dexter
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer with a genuine placed record on good ground (13/15 sim-going, 1W7P), but Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero's nine-year-old will be competing for the same territory as several hold-up rivals; tongue-tie and blinkers suggest he needs everything to fall right, and being pushed forward from his natural role blunts his edge.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Bangor-on-Dee last time when a run was required after a break, beaten 31 lengths; blinkers and tongue-tie both fitted for the first time now, and there may be more to offer off an eased mark — though he is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's mare has a solid pattern of placing (2W6P in 13 qualifying runs) and won a chase last season on good ground, but she is a true hold-up operator squeezed into a midfield role by the race's composition; off 32 days without a win recently, she needs the pace to collapse to find her best form — a scenario that carries only marginal probability here.
runners_data.comment: Third behind the pace at his last start, beaten 10 lengths off 90, and 1lb lower here with cheekpieces added; handles this going over 2m but his trainer has had a blank 14-day period and more is needed to feature in this company.

runners_data.name: Zumbi
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — disregard entirely; James Moffatt's other entry does not take part and has no bearing on the race shape or outcome.

races.paceDynamic: Bentley Road is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner handicap chase over 2m1½f at Cartmel, and with no natural rival to press her, Derek Fox can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Conquer The Breeze and Dream Jet are legitimate prominent types who will track closely, meaning the race is unlikely to be truly dawdled, but the pace should remain measured rather than frenetic on good ground. The field carries more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Cuzco Du Mathan, Dexter, and Clean Getaway are genuine hold-up types pushed into a midfield depiction, and in this shape they are unlikely to get a fully natural ride, which tempers their chances. A single-paced, controlled lead with prominent types tracking closely favours horses who can maintain rhythm close to the pace and challenge on the approach to the final fence, making the prominent/pressing profile the primary tactical beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Conquer The Breeze arrives on a four-race sequence including two wins, and if she slots in just behind Bentley Road and jumps fluently she could hit the front before the last with nothing able to match her — monitor closely as she is the most likely beneficiary of the dominant shape.

Bentley Road's ability to sustain her lead matters enormously for the shape of this race — if she makes a jumping error at any of the first five fences, the entire pace map resets and the prominent trackers could find themselves involved in a scramble rather than a patient stalk.

Ghasham and Fort Randall are the two best-credentialled horses trying to deliver from the hold-up position — if the gallop is genuinely honest, watch whether they can pick up down the far side or are left with too much ground to make up from the final bend.

Blue Reed's recent win came over 19f on good ground with similar headgear in place — she is the most interesting each-way profile among the prominent horses if Bentley Road and Conquer The Breeze burn each other off, as she may be cruising just outside the lead battle.

The three redistributed hold-up types (Cuzco Du Mathan, Dexter, Clean Getaway) will all be seeking the same late ground — watch for interference or crowding on the final bend if the field compresses, which could affect each other's finishing runs regardless of their individual merits.
